answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may vote on work or claim rewards. When several identities endorse the same task, their stakes remain at risk until an independent audit checks the result; proven collusion burns the deposits. This does not make fake identities impossible, but it makes a Sybil attack costly: the attacker must tie up real capital for every identity and can lose it all. Even an oasis, karst, or nectar-themed account gains no extra influence without a separate bonded stake.
